entries.text: What's Changed ℹ️ Scheduled jobs are now supported. A job is a one-shot unit of work declared in the top-level jobs: element of your Compose file, run on demand or on a schedule. Scheduling needs Docker Engine 29.10 or later with the jobs extension enabled (it is off by default: dockerd --extension-enable org.mobyproject.jobs.v0). Manual jobs keep working on any engine, and projects that declare no jobs are unaffected. services: db: image: postgres jobs: backup: image: backup-tool depends_on: [db] triggers: schedule: cron: "0 3 * * *" docker compose up (or create) registers the scheduled jobs with the engine, which fires them on its own clock; docker compose down removes them. On an engine without jobs support, up refuses a project with scheduled jobs before creating anything. docker compose run backup triggers a job right away: its dependencies start first, its logs are streamed and its exit code is returned. On an engine without jobs support, it runs as a one-off service with a warning, as before. ✨ Improvements Jobs Jobs: add support for one-shot and scheduled jobs by @glours in #14155 Full Changelog: v5.7.2...v5.8.0

entries.summary: ℹ️ Heads-up for users of Compose as a library: Up now runs its Create and Start phases as a single plan over a single daemon snapshot, for up -d (#14290) and interactive up (#14305), as scale, watch rebuilds and start…
entries.text: What's Changed ℹ️ Heads-up for users of Compose as a library: Up now runs its Create and Start phases as a single plan over a single daemon snapshot, for up -d (#14290) and interactive up (#14305), as scale, watch rebuilds and start already do (#14291, #14296). The CLI behaves as before. If you call api.Compose.Up from your own program: Up now validates its options first, with the same rules as the CLI flags: UpOptions.Validate() returns an *api.IncompatibleOptionsError (errors.Is(err, api.ErrIncompatibleOptions)) for Start.Wait combined with Start.Attach, and for a detached Up (no Start.Attach) combined with OnExit, ExitCodeFrom or Watch. Those combinations used to be silently ignored (#14306). Up works on the project it is given and ignores StartOptions.Project. The daemon is not observed again between the two phases: a container that exits after the plan is built is not started again, and one removed in between makes its start fail instead of being skipped. A planning error of the Start phase now fails before any container is created. A foreground Up now gives a use_api_socket service its /run/secrets/docker/config.json, as up -d does, and shows the output of pre_start hooks. The keyboard menu of an interactive up is no longer built by the library: set NavigationMenu: true and pass an implementation with compose.WithNavigationMenu(...), otherwise no menu is displayed and a warning says so (#14324). entries.text: update to go1.26.10 These releases include 1 security fix following the security policy: crypto/x509: mitigation for security concerns with a specific Certificate Authority We're blocking trust in a small set of intermediate certificates due to specific security concerns around their operation. Verify will now filter out chains which contain these intermediates, preventing them from being returned to the caller. We highly recommend immediately upgrading to this release. This is CVE-2026-111943 and Go issue https://go.dev/issue/82345. Full Changelog: v5.6.0...v5.6.1
